newsitem.title: FRANCE: Giscard wants parliamentary body with say on Euro.
newsitem.headline: Giscard wants parliamentary body with say on Euro.

text.p: Former French president Valery Giscard d'Estaing said on Friday a special parliamentary committee supervising the planned Euro currency should be appointed to balance the power of the European central bank.
In an interview with the newspaper Le Figaro, Giscard d'Estaing also expressed support for a stability pact ensuring financial rigour within the monetary union.

The committee on the euro should be composed of around 60 members, drawn from the European assembly and national parliaments, and should meet every three months to question the head of the European central bank, he said.
The committee would be on an ad hoc basis and consultative, running alongside the Ecofin council of finance ministers, he said.

"I think we should go to a system closer to the American Federal Reserve. The Fed regularly explains its policy to Congress, with two key references -- the risk of inflation and the level of economic activity," he said.
The countries expected to be in the first wave in the euro would be Germany, France and the Benelux states, with perhaps Austria and Finland, he said. "The real problem is Italy and Spain," he added.
He said "it was indispensable to have a stability pact with automatic fines for "bad pupils" except in exceptional circumstances such as a recession.
European Union leaders are meeting in Dublin today as part of the intergovernmental conference to prepare for monetary union. -- Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
